column2: How do I find an ancestor in a factory’s staff registers (Archives du monde du travail)?
column3: Lists → Employers → the employer’s record → “🏭 Staff registers (ANMT)…”: the Archives nationales du monde du travail in Roubaix keep the archives of many companies, searched by name. “⤒ Import…” (kind “Staff register”) adds to the record an occupation “Employer: …” (the person then appears in “The family at this employer”) and a line in the employer’s timeline.

column2: Where do I search for a railway worker, a gendarme or a police officer who died on duty?
column3: “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, “France — soldiers, railway workers, gendarmes, police officers” section. The exact addresses of these memorials could not be checked: the app launches a Google search of the name with the occupation; if you know the address of the memorial, write it in “⚙️ Site addresses”. On import, the death “Died on duty” is only suggested if the record does not already have a death.

column2: How do I find a record of a French person born, married or who died abroad (consular civil registration)?
column3: The registers of consulates and embassies are at the Archives diplomatiques in Nantes; they cannot be searched by name online. “🔍 Online archives…” → “Archives diplomatiques de Nantes” opens a FranceArchives search and copies the name for a request. The record received is imported as a “Record”.

column2: Where do I find the history of a village or a department (Geneawiki)?
column3: On a commune’s monograph (Charts) and on a village record: the “📖 Geneawiki: …” buttons open the page of the commune and that of the department on Geneawiki (online registers, archives, history, transcriptions).

column2: How do I search for a Soviet soldier or a victim of repression in the USSR?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…”, “Russia and USSR” section: Pamyat Naroda (soldiers of 1941-1945; write the name in Cyrillic for better results) and Memorial (victims of political repression). What comes from Memorial stays sober on the record (“Political repression (USSR)”) and a record that carries it never goes into a game, as for deportees.

column2: How do I date a photo using the photographer’s name?
column3: Treasures → “📷 Date an old photo” → “📷 The photographer…”: write the name and town printed on the back of the card, open the Daguerre database, Portrait Sépia or Gallica’s old directories, then paste the line that gives their years of activity (“active from 1862 to 1895”): “Put these years in the photo” adds them to the clues.

column2: Where do I search for the biography of an activist, a trade unionist or an elected official (Maitron)?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…” → “Maitron”: the whole biographical dictionary of the labour and social movement (not just those who were shot). Copy the entry and “⤒ Import…”: it becomes a note on the record, with the birth and death if they are missing.

column2: How do I find manuscripts or private archives about an ancestor (CCFr, Calames)?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…”, “France — manuscripts and private archives” section: the CCFr (manuscripts and collections of libraries) and Calames (universities). “⤒ Import…” (kind “Archive collection”) creates the source with the reference and the library, and a note if you tick it.

column2: How do I search the archives of 30 European countries (Archives Portal Europe)?
column3: “Search the Internet” block of the record → “🔍 Online archives…” → “🇪🇺 Europe” section: the search opens in your browser, with the name and the place already written. The portal searches the inventories of the archives of 30 countries: it tells you in which collection and under which reference a register is. The app never connects to the site. Then “⤒ Import what you found” stores the document, creates the source and suggests the record (nothing is replaced, “↶ Undo” removes everything).

column2: How do I find out whether an ancestor was recognised as “Righteous Among the Nations”?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…” → “🇫🇷 France — Righteous and war memorials” section → “Comité français pour Yad Vashem” (the name is copied for the site’s box). If you find their entry, “⤒ Import” adds the distinction to “🏆 Competitions and awards”, soberly, with the file and the note “to check”. A record recognised as “Righteous” no longer appears in the games or in the playable Treasures.

column2: How do I find the file of a foundling or a child in public care (Assistance publique)?
column3: On their record, “👶 Child in care” block → “👶 Search for their file”: Archives de Paris (foundlings and children in care) and, for the other departments, FranceArchives’ inventories. “⤒ Import the file…” stores the image, creates the source and adds a placement (register number, admission, wet nurse) next to those already noted; a placement with the same register number is kept as it is.

column2: How do I keep the photo of a commune’s war memorial (MonumentsMorts, University of Lille)?
column3: Charts → the commune’s monograph → “🌍 European archives, memorial, old cadastre, society…” → “MonumentsMorts” (the commune is copied). Save the photo, then “⤒ Import for this place…”: it is linked to the place (and to a record if you choose one), with its source. From a record’s “Military” block: “🗿 War memorial”.

column2: Where do I find the free transcriptions of a department’s genealogy society?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…” → “📒 Genealogy society transcriptions” section. Write the address of your society for each department in “⚙️ Site addresses” → “My genealogy society, by department”: it will open for anyone born in that department. Without an address, the app opens a search “genealogy society + department”, or the directory of the Fédération française de généalogie.

column2: How do I find out which registers exist for a village abroad (FamilySearch Wiki, GenWiki, GOV)?
column3: Charts → the place’s monograph → “🧭 How to search here (FamilySearch Wiki)”: the wiki says, for each country and often each parish, which registers exist, where they are and which are online. For Germany and Central Europe, the “🧭 Help searching in a place” section adds GenWiki (one page per village) and GOV (the old names and parishes of a place).

column2: How do I search for a German ancestor (CompGen, Archion)?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…” → “🇩🇪 Germany” section: the village family books (CompGen, free) and Archion, the registers of Protestant parishes, marked PAYING (subscription). Untick “Free only” to see the paying sites: they always stay at the end.

column2: Where can I see the old cadastre of a village in Bohemia, Moravia or Austria-Hungary?
column3: Place monograph → “🌍 European archives, memorial, old cadastre…” → “🗺 Central Europe”: Archivní mapy (cadastre of 1824-1843, free) and Mapire (maps of the Habsburg empire, partly paying). The name of the place is copied for the site’s box. Save the plan, then “⤒ Import for this place…” → “Cadastre plan”: it is linked to the place with its source.

column2: How do I search Hungarian newspapers (Arcanum ADT)?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…” → “🗺 Central Europe” section → “Arcanum ADT” (PARTLY PAYING: the search is free, reading often requires a subscription). An article found is imported like those from Gallica: it goes into the record’s “📰 In the media”.

column2: Can I use Ancestry for free?
column3: Yes, but only in a library: many libraries and departmental Archives offer “Ancestry Library Edition” on their computers. “🔍 Online archives…” → “🏛 In the library” prepares the search (“Free in the library” badge); open it on site. At home, the “Ancestry” button opens the paying version.

column2: How do I add my own site to “Search the Internet”, try it and share it?
column3: Settings → Appearance → “Search the Internet” → “My sites”: the site’s name, its search address with {nom}, {prenom}, {lieu}, {annee_naissance}, {annee_deces}, {de}, {a}, {conjoint} or {departement} in place of what is searched for, its section and an icon. “🧪 Try” shows the address filled in with the open record (or an example) and opens it. “💾 Saved settings” keeps your list under a name; ⋯ → Export makes it a file to give away, which is opened with “⤒ Import”.

column2: Where do I find old books and newspapers about my region (Normannia, Yroise, Rosalis, Numelyo…)?
column3: On a village record (or a commune’s monograph), under the figures: the app suggests the digital library of its region — Numelyo and Lectura Plus (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes), Rosalis (Toulouse, Occitanie), Mémoire vive (Besançon, Bourgogne-Franche-Comté), Normannia (Normandy), Yroise (Brest, Brittany). “↗” opens the search in your browser with the name of the place; “📚 Other libraries…” shows all the others, arranged by region. From a record: “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”. If the site’s page finds nothing, “search this site with Google”. A page found is imported with “⤒ Import…”: it is linked to the place (or the person), with its source “to check”.

column2: My ancestor wrote a book: how do I find their author record (IdRef, data.bnf.fr)?
column3: On the record of a person who published (a book or a work in their record) or who has an artist, writer, scholar, inventor… profile, the “✍️ IdRef · data.bnf (author)” button appears in “Search the Internet” and in the blocks of their profiles. The author record opens in your browser. Copy its text, or save it (IdRef: “Download” as XML or JSON; data.bnf: “Save as…”), then “⤒ Import…”: the app reads their dates and places of birth and death, shows you “Is this the same person?”, suggests the birth and death only if they are missing (nothing is replaced), and adds the link to their “Online records”. “↶ Undo” removes everything.

column2: How do I search for a name in transcribed old texts (Wikisource)?
column3: “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…” → “Wikisource — search in the texts”: the full-text search opens with the name in quotation marks (and the place if you have written it). Wikisource transcribes books, directories, newspapers: a notable ancestor may be mentioned there.

column2: My ancestor was a sailor: where are his maritime registration records?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…” → “Seafarers” section: write his home port (Saint-Malo, Fécamp, Sète…). The app says which maritime district the quarter belonged to, which centre of the Service historique de la Défense (Cherbourg, Brest, Lorient, Rochefort, Toulon) keeps its registers, and gives the link to the departmental Archives of the port, where many registers have been transferred. This is an indicative breakdown: check on the site. What you find is imported as “Registered seaman” (Military block).

column2: How do I read a reference from the Minutier central of Paris notaries (MC/ET/XLVIII/312)?
column3: MC = Minutier central, ET = étude (office), then the number of the office in Roman numerals (XLVIII = 48), then the article (the bundle). “🔍 Online archives…” → “Paris notaries” opens the search at the Archives nationales and the Salle des inventaires virtuelle; a record found is imported as “Notarial deed (Minutier central)”: marriage contract, probate inventory, will.
